en.name: Indexing & Query Plans
en.description: How the planner actually chooses, and why your index is ignored.

id.name: Indexing & Query Plan
id.description: Cara planner benar-benar memilih, dan kenapa index kamu diabaikan.

en.stem_md: You have `CREATE INDEX idx ON bookings (status, created_at)`. Which query can use that index for the filter **and** the sort, with no separate sort step?
en.explanation_md: Leftmost prefix rule: a composite index is only usable left to right, with no gaps.

id.stem_md: Kamu punya index `CREATE INDEX idx ON bookings (status, created_at)`. Query mana yang bisa memakai index itu untuk filter **dan** sort sekaligus, tanpa langkah sort terpisah?
id.explanation_md: Leftmost prefix rule: index komposit hanya berguna dari kolom paling kiri ke kanan, tanpa bolong.

en.option_explanation_md: The leading column is skipped, so the index is only reachable through a full index scan.

id.option_explanation_md: Kolom paling kiri dilewati, jadi index hanya bisa dipakai lewat full index scan.

en.option_explanation_md: One value on the first column, then ordered by the second. The index is already in that order, and a backward scan is free.

id.option_explanation_md: Satu nilai di kolom pertama, lalu urut di kolom kedua. Index sudah terurut begitu, backward scan pun gratis.

en.option_explanation_md: Two status values means two separately ordered ranges. The planner still has to merge or sort.

id.option_explanation_md: Dua nilai status berarti dua rentang terurut terpisah. Planner masih harus merge atau sort.

en.label_md: `ORDER BY created_at, status` with no WHERE
en.option_explanation_md: Column order is reversed from the index, and there is no filter.

id.option_explanation_md: Urutan kolom kebalik dari index, dan tanpa filter.

en.stem_md: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on a report page produces this. What does it tell you?
en.code_snippet:
-> Nested Loop  (actual time=0.004..214.9 rows=8412 loops=1)
      -> Seq Scan on bookings  (rows=8412 loops=1)
      -> Index Scan using users_pkey  (rows=1 loops=8412)
en.explanation_md: The first thing to read in EXPLAIN is not cost, it is loops and the gap between estimated and actual rows.

id.stem_md: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` sebuah halaman laporan mengeluarkan baris ini. Apa artinya?
id.code_snippet:
-> Nested Loop  (actual time=0.004..214.9 rows=8412 loops=1)
      -> Seq Scan on bookings  (rows=8412 loops=1)
      -> Index Scan using users_pkey  (rows=1 loops=8412)
id.explanation_md: Yang dibaca pertama di EXPLAIN bukan cost, tapi loops dan selisih estimated vs actual rows.

en.label_md: The `users_pkey` index is unused and needs a `REINDEX`
en.option_explanation_md: The index is being used. The problem is how many times it is called.

id.label_md: Index `users_pkey` tidak terpakai dan perlu di-`REINDEX`
id.option_explanation_md: Index justru terpakai. Masalahnya berapa kali dia dipanggil.

en.label_md: A nested loop doing one lookup per outer row — an N+1 that moved into the planner
en.option_explanation_md: `loops=8412` means that index scan ran 8,412 times. Correct result, expensive total.

id.label_md: Nested loop yang menjalankan satu lookup per baris outer — N+1 yang pindah ke dalam planner
id.option_explanation_md: `loops=8412` artinya index scan itu dieksekusi 8.412 kali. Benar hasilnya, mahal totalnya.

en.option_explanation_md: A reasonable distractor, but estimated and actual rows match here.

id.option_explanation_md: Distraktor yang masuk akal, tapi estimasi dan actual rows di sini cocok.

en.label_md: The `bookings` table is missing an index on its foreign key
en.option_explanation_md: The seq scan on bookings is intentional, since every row is needed.

id.label_md: Tabel `bookings` kekurangan index pada foreign key
id.option_explanation_md: Seq scan pada bookings disengaja karena semua baris dibutuhkan.

en.stem_md: Two workers run this block at the same time on PostgreSQL at the default `READ COMMITTED`. Balance starts at 100, both deduct 50. What is the final balance?
en.explanation_md: Three fixes: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, an atomic `SET balance = balance - 50`, or a `version` column for optimistic locking.

id.stem_md: Dua worker menjalankan blok ini bersamaan di PostgreSQL dengan isolation default `READ COMMITTED`. Saldo awal 100, keduanya memotong 50. Berapa saldo akhirnya?
id.explanation_md: Perbaikannya ada tiga: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, `SET balance = balance - 50` yang atomik, atau kolom `version` untuk optimistic locking.

en.option_explanation_md: That is what you expect, not what happens.

id.option_explanation_md: Itu yang kamu harapkan, bukan yang terjadi.

en.label_md: 50 — the second transaction overwrites with a value computed from stale data
en.option_explanation_md: A lost update. Both read 100, both write 50. One deduction vanishes with no error.

id.label_md: 50 — transaksi kedua menimpa dengan nilai hasil hitungan data basi
id.option_explanation_md: Lost update. Keduanya membaca 100, keduanya menulis 50. Satu pemotongan hilang tanpa error.

en.label_md: The second transaction fails with a serialization error

id.label_md: Transaksi kedua gagal dengan serialization error

en.option_explanation_md: No conflict is detected, so nothing is rolled back.

id.option_explanation_md: Tidak ada konflik yang terdeteksi, jadi tidak ada yang di-rollback.

en.stem_md: The `/api/v1/leaderboard` response is cached in Redis for 60 seconds. At a peak of 4,000 req/s, the moment the key expires database CPU pins at 100% for two seconds. Which fix is right?
en.explanation_md: Three patterns worth memorising: a lock around the rebuild, refresh-ahead before expiry, and jittered TTLs so keys do not expire in lockstep.

id.stem_md: Endpoint `/api/v1/leaderboard` di-cache 60 detik di Redis. Saat puncak 4.000 req/s, tepat ketika key expire, CPU database melonjak 100% selama dua detik. Perbaikan mana yang benar?
id.explanation_md: Tiga pola yang perlu dihafal: lock saat rebuild, refresh-ahead sebelum expire, dan TTL yang di-jitter supaya key tidak expire serempak.

en.label_md: Drop the TTL to 10 seconds so the data stays fresher
en.option_explanation_md: That makes it worse: a stampede every 10 seconds instead of every 60.

id.label_md: Turunkan TTL jadi 10 detik supaya datanya lebih segar
id.option_explanation_md: Memperparah: stampede yang tadinya tiap 60 detik jadi tiap 10 detik.

en.label_md: Add a short lock — one request rebuilds the value while the rest serve the stale copy
en.option_explanation_md: This is a cache stampede, and the cure is letting exactly one rebuild through. Redis `SET NX EX` is enough.

id.label_md: Pasang lock singkat — satu request membangun ulang nilainya, sisanya menyajikan salinan basi
id.option_explanation_md: Ini cache stampede, dan obatnya memang satu rebuild saja yang lewat. Redis `SET NX EX` cukup.

en.label_md: Move the cache into process memory on each app server
en.option_explanation_md: Now you have N copies expiring at nearly the same time, and servers can disagree.

id.label_md: Pindahkan cache ke memory proses di setiap app server
id.option_explanation_md: Jadi N salinan yang expire hampir bersamaan, plus data antar server bisa beda.

en.label_md: Add a read replica to absorb the query spike
en.option_explanation_md: Treating the symptom with hardware. The spike still happens.

id.label_md: Tambah read replica untuk menampung lonjakan query
id.option_explanation_md: Mengobati gejala dengan hardware. Lonjakannya tetap terjadi.
